# choices.md — the build's choices where the design is unclear or leaves a case open (J156)

The design is a reference, not a contract. Where it is unclear, or the fix list leaves a case open, the seat that meets
the case picks, records the pick here and names the test that holds it; the tests judge. One row per choice; rows are
append-only (a reversal is a new row naming the row it replaces). A choice that changes the design's text is also routed
to the fix list, and the design is corrected later from it.

Columns: **id** · **date** · **seat** · **design section** · **the choice** · **the reason** · **the test that holds it**.

Clipper2's booleans run through its **double** API (precision 10⁻³ cm) and are snapped by the kernel's `snap`: its integer API truncates every new intersection point toward zero — up to 1 cm on each axis, measured on this machine — which put the two oracles 0.95 cm/cm apart on dense xor cases, where §3.2 (1) rounds to the nearest lattice point (0.089 cm/cm after the change). The library's missing declaration is a local `declare module` typing its default export as returning `unknown`, narrowed to the adapter's own interfaces; no library type reaches an exported signature (C-0124 (2), N-15). (2) *Fill rules on polygon-clipping*, which has no fill parameter and reads a self-crossing ring by the non-zero rule: non-zero — an operand's rings joined into one ring by doubled bridges from its first ring's first vertex (winding numbers add; each bridge, traversed once each way, adds none); even-odd — the XOR of the operand's simple rings (exact test on the kernel's `orient2d`) and of the fan triangles of each non-simple ring (crossing parity adds over any split of the boundary into closed paths). Every polygon-clipping call runs under the four exact quarter turns of the plane in turn (identity first), the result turned back, because its sweep in doubles throws on some near-degenerate inputs; only when all four throw is the case a typed oracle failure. (3) *Faces after snapping:* a face is a connected piece of the region's interior: the snapped rings are canonicalised by polygon-clipping's non-zero union and its output polygons of positive area counted — so two faces touching at a point count two however a library wrote them, a hole touching its outline counts none (the loop count of the representation is the fallback when the canonicalisation throws).
